newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Prague okays sale of IPB stake to Nomura.
newsitem.headline: Prague okays sale of IPB stake to Nomura.

text.p: The Czech government has given the go-ahead for Japan's Nomura Securities Co Ltd International to buy a 36 percent state stake in the third largest Czech bank, IPB a.s. and the deal should be done by August 1, a government spokesman said on Thursday.
"The government has approved the sale...which should be completed by August 1," spokesman Ivo Strejcek said without elaborating.
Nomura had been widely tipped to win the tender which was fought out between it and Dutch ING Bank NV.
The state holds a 34.48 percent stake in IPB through the privatisation agency, the National Property Fund (NPF), and an additional 4.45 percent via the Czech Post Office.

Investors and international organisations have long been calling on the Czech government to push on with the privatisation of Czech banks which are generally perceived as lacking the competitive edge of foreign rivals.

Finance Minister Ivan Pilip on Tuesday said he would submit proposals to the government for further state divestment in the other largest Czech banks -- Komercni Banka a.s., Ceska Sporitelna a.s. and Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s.-- on August 20.

Nomura already controls a five percent stake in IPB through the Czech-registered firm Nutshell s.r.o.. It has held as much as 10 percent of IPB, but recently let go of half of its holdings as part of a repurchase operation with shareholders.

The sale was delayed by a Finance Ministry investigation into IPB's investment subsidiary, Prvni Investicni a.s. (PIAS) PIAS, the Czech Republic's largest fund manager, was earlier this month fined 10 million crowns ($290,000), the maximum, for illegal financing operations and other violations.
The ministry also ordered changes in the management of PIAS and said it must cancel its contract making IPB its broker.

The privatisation process of IPB had already hit a snag when police arrested the bank's general director Jiri Tesar and his deputy for alleged fraud. The two have since been released from jail, but an investigation into the case continues. Tesar stepped down as director at IPB's annual general meeting.
IPB posted an 858 million crown net profit in 1996, according to Czech accounting standrds, which it has said it expects to rise to 2.03 billion this year.
